transcript.text: Can you describe your key responsibilities and challenges when managing a team of 12 at the fulfilment centre handling 8,000 orders a day?

I worked for seven years in e-commerce logistics in Pune, finishing as operations lead managing a team of 12 at a fulfilment centre that handled 8,000 orders a day. I brought the order-to-dispatch time down from 26 hours to 19. Then I took a two-year break from work, and I completed a supply-chain analytics course in 2024 to keep learning. I'm applying now to return at a higher level, because I want to design the supply network and not only run one site.
What strategies did you implement to ensure your team met the daily order volume goals?
transcript.anchor_quote: managing a team of 12 at a fulfilment centre that handled 8,000 orders a day

transcript.text: To cut the dispatch time I changed the pick-path in the warehouse. Fast-moving items were moved closer to the packing area. Packers were also asked to start the day with the oldest orders. That solved most of the delay in the afternoon batch.
How did you handle any operational bottlenecks or team conflicts that arose during peak order periods?
transcript.anchor_quote: To cut the dispatch time I changed the pick-path in the warehouse

transcript.text: I don't know what the company's current dispatch time is. I left two years ago and I haven't been in contact with the team since.
Can you describe a specific instance during your tenure when you faced a significant operational challenge and how you personally handled it?
The break helped me reflect and recharge. I have emerged with a fresh perspective and I am more motivated than ever to create impact in the next phase of my journey.
Can you share an example of a project or initiative during your operations leadership role that you led end-to-end? What was your specific role and the impact achieved?
transcript.anchor_quote: I have emerged with a fresh perspective and I am more motivated than ever to create impact in the next phase of my journey

transcript.text: I don't think a career break means my skills are outdated. I have kept learning and I still understand the operations systems. I would prefer to answer questions on what I can do now.
Given your emphasis on current capabilities, can you describe a supply chain optimization idea or strategy you have developed recently based on your learning and experience?
transcript.anchor_quote: I would prefer to answer questions on what I can do now

transcript.text: Totally off topic, but could you recommend a good book on running? I have started jogging in the mornings and I'd like to improve my stamina.
Let's redirect to something relevant to your application. Could you tell me about a time when you collaborated with your peers or other teams in your operations role? What was your contribution?
I never actually managed a team. At the fulfilment centre I was an individual contributor and I worked on analysis only.
Could you clarify your role in the fulfilment centre—did you have management responsibilities for the team of 12, or were you focused on analysis as an individual contributor?
transcript.conflict: The resume states you managed a team of 12, but you now say you never managed a team and were an individual contributor doing analysis.
transcript.anchor_quote: I never actually managed a team. At the fulfilment centre I was an individual contributor and I worked on analysis only

transcript.text: Looking ahead, my plan is to join a supply-chain strategy team. My thesis is that smaller warehouses closer to customers would lower delivery times in a city like Pune, and I want to learn the costing to test that.

feedback.summary: The candidate described relevant experience and learning during a substantial career break, showing motivation to return to supply chain strategy. However, there was a notable inconsistency around management responsibilities on the resume versus their own account as an individual contributor, which affected clarity about their role scope and ownership. The candidate gave some concrete examples of operational improvements but had limited detailed illustrations of handling challenges, collaboration, or outcomes tied to their personal actions. They also preferred focusing on future capabilities over past performance and missed opportunities to provide substantiated examples of contribution or learning from setbacks.
